fix(startup): real fallback timer, g-then-letter always on, no help over a dialog

- whenNear used requestIdleCallback's timeout as its fallback, which is a
  deadline, so the contact form and About stats started at the first idle moment
  whatever the page showed; use a real timer
- g then h/a/p/c lived in the deferred keyboard-help module, so a g c pressed
  while it downloaded lost both keys (or the prefix if the module landed
  between them); it needs nothing from the module, so it moves to main.js
- a ? pressed while help loaded could open it on top of the palette; check for
  an open dialog before requesting help and again when the module arrives

Tests: g c and the 1.2 s prefix before the module loads, the module landing
between the two keys, g ignored while the palette is open, a dialog opened
while help loads, and the contact form not loading merely because the
browser is idle (each mutation-checked).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #250 from and3rn3t/feat/home-about

feat(home): About, Experience and Writing (Phase 10.3b)

fix(dialogs): a section jump closes help; short screens scroll; one toast, announced inside a dialog

- g then a letter, pressed while keyboard help is open, jumped to a section the
  modal made inert, so focus could not land there and help stayed open: close
  help first
- the help dialog clipped its lower shortcuts on a very short screen: let it
  scroll vertically
- the palette had its own toast in the same place as the page's, so both could
  paint over each other: the palette now uses the page's one toast
- the toast is outside any open modal dialog, so it is inert there and its
  messages (offline, site updated) were not announced: each dialog carries an
  empty live region and the message is said there too while it is open

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(zone): reject unrecognised arguments instead of selecting every group

--only=tls and a misspelt flag were ignored, so a scoped --apply wrote every group.
parseArgs now walks the arguments, accepts both --only tls and --only=tls, and throws on
anything else.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #257 from and3rn3t/feat/og-manifest

feat(brand): share card, browser bar and manifest colours (Phase 10.5c)

fix: lock contact fields while sending, and derive slugs from the repo

- contact-form: fields are read-only while the request is out, so an edit
  can't be lost to reset()
- projectView: slug comes from github_repo's basename before metadata.name,
  so the palette and the generator agree
- contact-form.spec: match Formspree by hostname (CodeQL regex anchor)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(presence): review fixes - close on any message, no metrics, isolated e2e

- The Presence object closes a socket at the first message that reaches it:
  the runtime answers "ping" itself, so anything else is not our client, and
  each message would wake the billed object.
- A browser that refuses to build the WebSocket no longer breaks the page:
  presence stops for good, and the edge receipt starts first regardless.
- Presence handshakes are not written to portfolio_metrics (they carried the
  visitor's Cloudflare location and a browser/agent guess).
- e2e: the Worker mock is a function (mockWorker) usable on a page or a
  context. The two specs that build their own contexts now use it, so no
  run reaches the deployed Worker (they did: views, edge, presence), and a
  unit test fails if a spec builds its own context without it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(transitions): clear view-transition names once a transition is over

The names were set for a navigation and never removed, so a theme switch
captured the named elements separately, and after going back and opening a
different project two cards could share a name, which makes the browser skip
the transition. Clear the names when the transition settles (skipped or
finished), clear leftovers before naming, and clear on a back/forward-cache
restore. Tests record the names during a real navigation and fail on the old
script.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(offline): make the browser-bar colour follow a saved theme

The two theme-color tags are keyed to the OS colour scheme, and the page's
bootstrap applied a saved theme only to data-theme, so a visitor whose saved
choice differed from their OS got a bar that did not match the page. The
bootstrap now points both tags at the colour of the theme actually shown, and
leaves the OS-specific pair alone when nothing is saved.
